August 19, 2025

Attn:  Dr. Steven L. Lieberman, Acting Under Secretary for Health 
Department of Veterans Affairs
810 Vermont Avenue NW
Washington, DC 20420
Phone:  (202) 461-0373

Dear Acting Under Secretary Lieberman,
I am Dr. Earl Stewart, Jr. I am an Internal Medicine Physician and serve as the Medical Director of Health Equity for a large comprehensive health system in the State of Georgia.  I have trained in part as a medical student and resident physician at the VA Medical Centers in Murfreesboro, TN, Nashville, TN, and Providence, Rhode Island.  I am the son of a veteran, son-in-law of a veteran, nephew of veterans, and grandson of veterans.  I care for many veterans and their family members as a primary care physician in my clinical practice. I am writing on my own behalf to express my strong opposition to the Department of Veterans Affairs’ proposed rule to reinstate the full exclusion on abortions and abortion counseling from the VA medical benefits package, as well as the proposed reinstatement of these exclusions for the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA), both of which were removed in 2022.

As a physician dedicated to creating and advancing health equity, I am deeply concerned that reinstating these exclusions would significantly harm the health and well-being of veterans and their families. The evidence is clear that restricting access to abortion services and counseling disproportionately impacts those who already face barriers to care, including women, gender-diverse individuals, and people of color who have served our country.
A recent article in JAMA Health Forum (doi:10.1001/jamahealthforum.2022.4621) highlights the critical role that the VA’s 2022 policy change played in expanding access to essential reproductive health services for veterans, particularly those living in states with restrictive abortion laws. The article underscores that removing these exclusions improved health outcomes and reduced disparities among veterans.
Research published in Contraception (doi:10.1016/j.contraception.2017.09.012) demonstrates that lack of access to abortion services leads to increased health risks, including higher rates of maternal morbidity and mortality. This is especially concerning for veterans, who may have complex medical and mental health needs.

The Center for Reproductive Rights (https://reproductiverights.org/fact-sheet-abortion-access-veterans/) provides further evidence that veterans are more likely to experience unintended pregnancies and face unique barriers to reproductive care. Denying abortion coverage through VA and CHAMPVA would force many veterans to seek care outside the system, often at great personal and financial cost, or to carry pregnancies to term against their wishes or medical advice.

A recent study in the American Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajog.2024.09.003) found that abortion restrictions are associated with delayed and reduced access to care, leading to worse health outcomes for patients. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) also emphasizes in its 2024 committee statement (https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-statement/articles/2024/12/health-care-for-women-and-gender-diverse-active-duty-and-reserve-uniformed-service-members-and-veterans) that comprehensive reproductive health care, including abortion, is essential for the health and readiness of service members and veterans.

Additionally, research (doi:10.1055/s-0039-1678749) has shown that abortion counseling is a critical component of patient-centered care, supporting informed decision-making and improving mental health outcomes.
In summary, reinstating the exclusions on abortion and abortion counseling in VA and CHAMPVA benefits would undermine the health, autonomy, and dignity of veterans and their families. The evidence overwhelmingly supports maintaining access to comprehensive reproductive health care, including abortion and counseling, as a matter of health equity and justice.

Thank you for considering my testimony in recognition of the reproductive health needs of the veterans who so valiantly protect the freedoms we enjoy and the families that love and support them steadfastly.

Sincerely,
Earl Stewart, Jr., M.D., FACP
Internal Medicine Physician
Medical Director of Health Equity
